name: Orange-Rufous
lede: Orange-Rufous is a deep, burnt orange carried over from Ridgway's 1886 color nomenclature into his fuller 1912 system, and measured in our color graph as identical to a separately sourced Rust Orange.

sections.title: From an 1886 list to 1912's plates
sections.body:
The name first appears in Ridgway's 1886 *Nomenclature of Colors for Naturalists*, and was carried over into his fuller 1912 *Color Standards and Color Nomenclature* at plate II, hue 11, tone i [1]. The ISCC-NBS system later filed it as a deep orange, and Maerz and Paul's 1930 dictionary separately dated a chip for it to 1886 as well [1]. Our color graph finds a separately recorded name, Rust Orange, at zero units of difference, an exact duplicate under a different name [2].

Its nearest distinct relatives in the graph are [[signal-orange]], almost the same, and [[alloy-orange]] and [[burnt-orange]], both close behind [3].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: In our archive of 23,781 paintings, as photographed, a color within six units of Orange-Rufous covers at least five per cent of a canvas in 163 works, more common than 66 per cent of our named colors [4]. It peaks in the 1300s, in 5 of 251 paintings, at 2.2 times the archive's overall rate, and is most over-represented in paintings from India, at 4.0 times expected [4]. The earliest dated appearance in our archive is the year 1000, nearly nine centuries before the name's own 1886 record, a look-alike hue, not proof of pigment, a floor and not a first, since the archive's early centuries are thin [4]. These remain photographs of aged, varnished paintings, read as screen colors [4].
